instantiated_cells.justification: The statute defines lobbying as "communicat[ing] directly or through his or her agents" for the purpose of influencing action, without enumerating specific activity modes (oral, written, electronic, etc.).

The statute defines lobbyist, lobbying firm (any business entity including individual contract lobbyists, partnerships, etc.), and lobbyist employer broadly to include persons employing lobbyists or contracting for lobbying services; "person" includes firms, partnerships, corporations, and associations, capturing professional lobbyists, in-house lobbyists for companies/organizations, consultancies, and law firms; public entities/government agencies are excluded per §86300(a).
The Definitions chapter provided contains no definition of "public entity"; §82047 defines "person" and §82048 defines "public official," but neither defines "public entity."

The lobbying firm definition includes a materiality test requiring that "a substantial or regular portion of the activities" be for influencing legislative or administrative action, and §82039 includes a monetary threshold ($2,000/month) operating as a materiality filter.

The lobbyist definition expressly covers communications with "any elective state official, agency official, or legislative official" for influencing legislative or administrative action, which covers state legislators and executive officials including the Governor (whose actions are legislative action per §82037).

Targets include elective state officials, agency officials (executive branch/bureaucracy), and legislative officials (defined in §82038 as employees/consultants of the Legislature, i.e., staff); §82037 includes the Governor's action on bills.
Same as row_005: definition covers communications with elective state officials, agency officials, and legislative officials, encompassing legislators and executive officials including the Governor.
Same as row_005: definition covers communications with elective state officials, agency officials, and legislative officials.
Same as row_005: definition covers communications with elective state officials, agency officials, and legislative officials.
Targets include elective state officials, agency officials (executive/bureaucracy), and legislative officials (Legislature employees/consultants/staff); §82037 captures Governor's bill approval.
The statute exempts elected public officials acting in their official capacity and state employees acting within scope of employment from registration as lobbyists.

Public employees are addressed: §86300(a) exempts state employees within scope of employment but imposes a $10/month gift cap; the lobbyist definition uses a compensation threshold ($2,000/month) and "principal duties" time standard.
The lobbying definitions rely on compensation thresholds and direct-communication activities, not on any public charter or special government protection criterion.
The definitions of lobbyist, lobbying firm, and lobbyist employer do not rely on ownership criteria; they rely on compensation and communication activity.
The definitions do not rely on the structure or composition of revenue; they rely on receipt of compensation for influencing legislative/administrative action and direct communication activities.
